ratings_why.fun: Winding a visible moon to pick your shop phase and your fight phase is a real choice every turn, and Full Moons pay out in permanent stats you can watch land.
ratings_why.distinct: A shared phase clock plus text-borrowing plays unlike any of today's tribes, though Borrow's power comes mostly from other tribes' cards.

verdict_why: The core reads well, but Grandam of the Forms and Borrow's stacking with Dame Waxwell don't say what happens, and a player can't predict them.

points.text: Grandam of the Forms: say what a Leveret with no Hare in front does, and whether the copy has the Hare's stats plus the Leveret's gains or only the gains.
A Ribboned Jack borrowing Dame Waxwell: does it make triggers fire three times, or twice still? Write the stacking rule into Borrow.
Borrow reads only if the card shows the lent text with a source marker while Full; build that into the card frame from the start, as the design itself warns.
Old Wat: say whether he returns as Bought (sells for 1 again) or Created (0); as written he may be a free gold each turn.
Waning has only Dusk Nurse; a second Waning card, such as a boxing jill who hits harder as the moon fades, would make every phase a phase you build for.

standouts.why: Jill Longshanks boxing the enemy across is the seed's March boxing in one line, and Moonlit makes the full moon visibly hers.
The Three Hares shares its gains with both neighbours: the church-roof icon turned into a rule anyone can read.
Moon-Gazer is a Tier 1 whose whole text is one clear verb, and it teaches the tribe's main action.

weakest.why: Grandam's text is the hardest on the list to follow and leaves cases open.
Spring Jill is a plain Moonlit Bristle body; fine, but no story beyond a keyword.
The Leveret's 'left one of the two, or the right if empty' rule is a fiddly read for a token that appears often.

flags.note: Copy rule and the no-Hare-in-front case aren't defined.
Stacking with a Borrower that borrows Waxwell is undefined.
Bought or Created on return decides whether he farms gold.
Silverpenny borrowing another tribe's Tier 6 capstone with no Full-moon limit could run away.
With Waxwell and Ring Referee, Full every turn stacks fast; worth the owner's eye.
